prompt:
Warm editorial ink-and-wash illustration on a warm cream ground: a loose confident ink line with soft transparent watercolour washes over it, a muted earth palette of cream, rust, ochre, mustard, sage and warm grey, quiet and hand-made, the register of a good printed picture book. NOT neon, NOT 3D or CGI or Pixar, NOT glossy plastic, NOT neo-comic, NOT photoreal. EMPTY SET PLATE, ABSOLUTELY NO PEOPLE anywhere in this image. A corner of an ordinary family house that has been turned into a desk, seen from inside the room at seated eye height. A plain wooden table stands against the wall under a SASH WINDOW with daylight coming through it. A mismatched wooden dining chair is pulled out. On the wall, a child's crayon drawing stuck up with tape. A shelf of well-read children's picture books with broken spines. A cooling mug, a few loose papers, ordinary cables that are just cables. A radiator under the window. Through an open DOORWAY AT THE LEFT you can see a bit of hallway and the corner of a sofa with a toy on the floor. LIVED-IN and untidy and warm. It is NEVER an office, NEVER a studio, NEVER a workshop, NEVER a wall of monitors, NEVER a whiteboard of diagrams, NEVER impressive, NEVER styled, NEVER dramatically lit. THE DESK IS EMPTY OF ANY COMPUTER: no laptop, no screen, no monitor at all. RENDER ONE MOMENT IN TIME: one view of one room, never a split panel. Render ONE single image only: NOT a contact sheet, NOT a grid, NOT a turnaround strip. No panel borders, no captions, no labels, no text of any kind.

DEVICE ANATOMY, NON-NEGOTIABLE: any phone, laptop, tablet or monitor is anatomically correct. The GLOWING DISPLAY is on the SCREEN side, and that side FACES ITS USER. A person looking at a device sees its screen; the viewer therefore sees the device's BACK or EDGE plus the light it throws onto the user's face and hands. NEVER put the screen image on the back of a phone, on a laptop's outer lid, or on a monitor's rear. NEVER show a screen facing the camera while the person using it looks at the opposite side. If both the user's face and the screen content must be visible, shoot it over the user's shoulder.

READABLE SURFACES FACE THEIR READER: any book, page, letter, scroll or sign a character is reading or writing faces THAT CHARACTER, never the camera. Compose over-the-shoulder or from behind so the surface genuinely faces them. Any handwriting is abstract handwriting-like line work with NO real readable letters.

NO USER INTERFACE ANYWHERE: no windows, menu bars, buttons, icons, toolbars, panels, form fields, cursors, floating rectangles or screenshot-like elements. Screens carry only soft glow or vague painterly shapes.
